proposals.before: Shi Hu sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
proposals.after: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
proposals.sourceQuote: 季龍又使石成入攻凡城，不克，進陷廣城。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, failed, then advanced and took Guangcheng; EN omits again (又).

proposals.before: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;
proposals.after: Moreover, when Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;
proposals.sourceQuote: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
proposals.sourceReason: Source: moreover Huang learned Yu Liang died and Bing and Yi succeeded as generals-ministers, then memorialized on muddled vs clear rulers who elevate the worthy together; EN drops 又 and softens 继为将相/昏明.

proposals.before: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
proposals.after: If one could change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided.
proposals.sourceQuote: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: if one can change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided; EN adds in time, which Chinese does not state.

proposals.before: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
proposals.after: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side, and recalling past affairs still burns with anguish to this day.
proposals.sourceQuote: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age and should exalt Jins Way, yet meets many state hardships, with deep grief pressing and past affairs still burning; EN merges 命世天挺 into one gloss.

proposals.before: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
proposals.after: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
proposals.sourceQuote: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: tracing the cause, late Minister of Works Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle held heavy power, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals so Su Jun and Zu Yue ruined the state; EN adds harshly.

proposals.before: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
proposals.after: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
proposals.sourceQuote: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: past events if not forgotten are a model for later affairs, yet Bing as Zhongshu jian and Left General with fellows holds central pivot and outer commands, brothers side by side unmatched; EN drops 不忘.

proposals.before: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
proposals.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and his fellows ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
proposals.sourceQuote: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty deeply honors Weiyang maternal-uncle ties; Bing and others ought themselves to stretch necks in expectation; EN replaces 渭阳 with generic family ties.

proposals.before: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
proposals.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
proposals.sourceQuote: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Huang often asks why not enfeoff maternal clan with vassal states, enrich stipends and gifts, and limit power and advantage so there is no partial favor above or private talk below; EN turns 何不 into an imperative and drops 利.

proposals.before: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
proposals.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
proposals.sourceQuote: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: servant and Bing and others differ in rank and are far apart in situation; as close imperial kin they warrant deference to circumstances; EN drops 等 and reorders speakers.

proposals.before: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
proposals.after: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold the rank of supreme general, worry day and night and know not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
proposals.sourceQuote: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: disheveled-hair foreign general worries day and night how to repay, can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and sincerity to answer state grace; EN truncates the closing clauses.

proposals.before: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
proposals.after: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant and he withdrew.
proposals.sourceQuote: 其年皝伐高句麗，王釗乞盟而還。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: that year Huang campaigned against Goguryeo; King Zhao begged a covenant and Huang returned; EN reduces 乞盟 to sued for peace.

proposals.before: Planning against the Shi, he told his commanders, “Shi Hu trusts his garrisons at Anle and neglects the open country north and south of the wall—a sudden raid could overrun the whole Ji plain.”
proposals.after: Huang was about to plan against the Shi clan; he calmly told the generals: “Shi Hu thinks the cities of Anle and the rest are strictly and heavily guarded, and surely sets no defenses north and south of the city; now if we take a deceitful route and strike where he does not expect, the whole northern territory of Ji can be broken.”
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
proposals.sourceReason: Source: planning against the Shi, Huang calmly told generals Shi Hu trusts Anle and the other cities heavy defenses so north and south of the city lack preparations; a deceitful route unexpected could break all northern Ji; EN misstates north/south of the wall and whole Ji plain, and drops 从容/诡路.

proposals.before: Emperor Cheng then sent Guo Xi to invest him as palace attendant, grand commander north of the river, grand general, and king of Yan, leaving other posts unchanged.
proposals.after: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.
proposals.sourceQuote: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang palace attendant, grand commander of military affairs north of the Yellow River, grand general, and King of Yan, other offices unchanged; EN drops concurrent Grand Herald and bearing credentials.

proposals.before: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
proposals.after: He took forty thousand picked soldiers through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and his son Murong Chui as vanguard, and sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.
proposals.sourceQuote: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: led 40,000 picked troops in from the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo; had Han and son Chui as vanguard; sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others with 15,000 advancing from Beizhi; EN drops 长史 and 等.

proposals.before: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
proposals.after: King Gao Zhao assumed Huang’s army was coming by the northern route, so he sent his younger brother Wu leading fifty thousand picked troops to block Beizhi, and personally led weaker troops to guard the southern defile.
proposals.sourceQuote: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: King Zhao thought Huang came by the northern route, so sent brother Wu with 50,000 picked troops to block Beizhi and personally led weak troops to guard the southern defile; EN drops 精锐.

proposals.before: Yuwen Gui sent Moqian Hun; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
proposals.after: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun against Huang; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
proposals.sourceQuote: 宇文歸遣其國相莫淺渾伐皝，諸將請戰，皝不許。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Yuwen Gui sent state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; generals asked to fight and Huang refused; EN omits 国相.

proposals.before: Murong Huang toured his domains, pushed farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
proposals.after: Murong Huang personally toured his prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝躬巡郡縣，勸課農桑，起龍城宮闕。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised Longcheng palace towers; EN drops 躬.

proposals.before: Yuwen Gui sent Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han; Huang sent word: “Sheyiyu is fierce—spar lightly until he grows reckless, then strike.”
proposals.after: Yuwen Gui sent his cavalry general Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han with the whole host; Huang sent word at a gallop: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; you ought to avoid him a little, wait until the bandits grow arrogant, then take them.”
proposals.sourceQuote: 歸使其騎將涉奕於盡眾距翰，皝馳遣謂翰曰：「奕於雄悍，宜小避之，待虜勢驕，然後取也。」
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Gui had cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host against Han; Huang sent word Sheyiyu is fierce and bold so slightly avoid him until the foe grows arrogant then take them; EN mistranslates 小避 as spar lightly.

proposals.before: He attacked, slew Sheyiyu, took his army, and drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe.
proposals.after: He then advanced to battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, and wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.
proposals.sourceQuote: 於是前戰，斬奕於，盡俘其眾，歸遠遁漠北。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: they advanced, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured the host; Gui fled far to the northern desert; EN makes Huang drive him rather than Gui flee.

proposals.before: He annexed a thousand li of pasture, resettled fifty thousand Yuwen dependents at Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu’s fort Weide.
proposals.after: He opened over a thousand li of territory, moved more than fifty thousand of their tribal settlements to Changli, and changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.
proposals.sourceQuote: 皝開地千餘里，徙其部人五萬餘落于昌黎，改涉奕於城為威德城。
proposals.sourceReason: Source: Huang opened over a thousand li, moved their division people over 50,000 settlements (落) to Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu city Weide; EN turns 落 into dependents.

sourceUnits.zh: 慕容皝
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝前軍帥慕容評敗季龍將石成等於遼西，斬其將呼延晃、張支，掠千餘戶以歸。
sourceUnits.en: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Shi Hu’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home more than a thousand households.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 段遼謀叛，皝誅之。
sourceUnits.en: When Duan Liao plotted revolt, Huang put him to death.
sourceUnits.literal: Duan Liao plotted rebellion; Huang executed him.

sourceUnits.zh: 季龍又使石成入攻凡城，不克，進陷廣城。
sourceUnits.en: Shi Hu sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Jilong again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, could not overcome it, advanced and took Guangcheng.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝雖稱燕王，未有朝命，乃遣其長史劉祥獻捷京師，兼言權假之意，並請大舉討平中原。
sourceUnits.en: Though he called himself King of Yan, he still lacked a court mandate, so he sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, explain his provisional assumption of authority, and ask for a major campaign to pacify the Central Plain.
sourceUnits.literal: Although Huang styled himself King of Yan, there was yet no court mandate; he thereupon sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, also explaining his provisional assumption of authority and requesting a great campaign to pacify the Central Plain.

sourceUnits.zh: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
sourceUnits.en: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;
sourceUnits.literal: Moreover, when he learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial, saying: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;

sourceUnits.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
sourceUnits.en: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.
sourceUnits.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.

sourceUnits.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
sourceUnits.en: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.
sourceUnits.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.

sourceUnits.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
sourceUnits.en: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.

sourceUnits.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.
sourceUnits.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
sourceUnits.en: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.
sourceUnits.literal: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in later regret.

sourceUnits.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne without effort.
sourceUnits.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang take the imperial throne without effort.

sourceUnits.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
sourceUnits.en: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!
sourceUnits.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!

sourceUnits.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
sourceUnits.en: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.
sourceUnits.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.

sourceUnits.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
sourceUnits.en: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.
sourceUnits.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.

sourceUnits.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
sourceUnits.en: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.
sourceUnits.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.

sourceUnits.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
sourceUnits.en: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
sourceUnits.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.

sourceUnits.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
sourceUnits.en: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.

sourceUnits.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
sourceUnits.en: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
sourceUnits.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.

sourceUnits.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
sourceUnits.en: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
sourceUnits.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!

sourceUnits.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
sourceUnits.en: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
sourceUnits.literal: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
sourceUnits.en: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

sourceUnits.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
sourceUnits.en: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!
sourceUnits.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!

sourceUnits.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
sourceUnits.en: Whence would slander spring!
sourceUnits.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!

sourceUnits.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!

sourceUnits.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
sourceUnits.en: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!
sourceUnits.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!

sourceUnits.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
sourceUnits.en: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
sourceUnits.en: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.

sourceUnits.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
sourceUnits.en: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!
sourceUnits.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!

sourceUnits.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and precautions were not taken at the first signs.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
sourceUnits.en: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.
sourceUnits.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.

sourceUnits.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
sourceUnits.en: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.
sourceUnits.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.

sourceUnits.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.

sourceUnits.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
sourceUnits.en: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.
sourceUnits.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
sourceUnits.en: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant wears disheveled hair in a foreign land, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
sourceUnits.en: If I do not speak, who will!
sourceUnits.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!

sourceUnits.zh: 又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。
sourceUnits.en: He also wrote to Yu Bing: By empress kinship and maternal closeness you hold the pivot, issue and receive royal commands, and with your brothers hold command and provincial posts, your network displayed across the capital region.
sourceUnits.literal: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.

sourceUnits.zh: 冰見表及書甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，遂與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王。
sourceUnits.en: On seeing the memorial and the letter, Yu Bing was greatly alarmed; because Huang was so far away and beyond his power to control, he joined He Chong and others in memorializing that Huang be allowed to style himself King of Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Bing, seeing the memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far away and beyond his power to control, he thereupon, with He Chong and the others, memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.

sourceUnits.zh: 其年皝伐高句麗，王釗乞盟而還。
sourceUnits.en: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
sourceUnits.literal: That year Huang campaigned against Gaogouli; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant, and Huang returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 明年，釗遣其世子朝於皝。
sourceUnits.en: The next year Gao Zhao sent his heir to pay homage to Huang.
sourceUnits.literal: The next year, Zhao sent his heir apparent to court at Huang.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
sourceUnits.en: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
sourceUnits.literal: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.

sourceUnits.zh: 歸信而不禁，故得周遊自任，至於山川形便，攻戰要路，莫不練之。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui trusted the act and left him free, so Han mapped every defile and road.
sourceUnits.literal: Gui believed and did not restrain; therefore was able to roam at will, reaching mountains and rivers’ forms and conveniences, attack and battle crucial roads—none not practiced.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。
sourceUnits.en: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che spoke nothing, stroked his breast only.

sourceUnits.zh: 車還以白，皝曰：「翰欲來也。」
sourceUnits.en: Wang Che reported the sign; Huang said, “He wants to come home.”
sourceUnits.literal: Che returned and reported; Huang said: “Han wishes to come.”

sourceUnits.zh: 乃遣車遺翰弓矢，翰乃竊歸駿馬，攜其二子而還。
sourceUnits.en: He sent Wang Che with a bow and arrows; Murong Han stole horses and rode back with his two sons.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon sent Che to present Han bow and arrows; Han then stole fine horses, carried his two sons and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
sourceUnits.en: Planning against the Shi, he told his commanders, “Shi Hu trusts his garrisons at Anle and neglects the open country north and south of the wall—a sudden raid could overrun the whole Ji plain.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang was about to plan the Shi clan; leisurely said to the generals: “Shi Jilong thinks the cities of Anle and the rest guard defense strict and heavy; surely north and south of the city he does not set equipment; now if by deceitful route go out where he does not expect, the whole north of Ji can be broken.”

sourceUnits.zh: 於是率騎二萬出蠮螉塞，長驅至於薊城，進渡武遂津，入于高陽，所過焚燒積聚，掠徙幽、冀三萬餘戶。
sourceUnits.en: He then led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford into Gaoyang, burning the stores wherever he passed, and carried off more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon he led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford, and entered Gaoyang; wherever he passed he burned the stores, and he plundered and relocated more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.

sourceUnits.zh: 使陽裕、唐柱等築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣。
sourceUnits.en: He had Yang Yu and Tang Zhu build Longcheng, raised palaces and shrines, and renamed Liucheng county Longcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Had Yang Yu, Tang Zhu, and others build Longcheng, construct palace and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng county.

sourceUnits.zh: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Cheng then sent Guo Xi to invest him as palace attendant, grand commander north of the river, grand general, and king of Yan, leaving other posts unchanged.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, King of Yan; the rest of offices all as before.

sourceUnits.zh: 封諸功臣百餘人，
sourceUnits.en: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.
sourceUnits.literal: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.

sourceUnits.zh: 咸康七年，皝遷都龍城。
sourceUnits.en: In the seventh year of Xiankang, he moved his capital to Longcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang, Huang moved the capital to Longcheng.

sourceUnits.zh: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
sourceUnits.en: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
sourceUnits.literal: Led picked soldiers forty thousand, entered from the southern defile to campaign against Yuwen and Goguryeo; again had Han and son Chui as vanguard, sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading host fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.

sourceUnits.zh: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
sourceUnits.en: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
sourceUnits.literal: Goguryeo King Zhao thought Huang’s army came by the northern route; thereupon sent his younger brother Wu leading picked fifty thousand to block Beizhi; personally led weak soldiers to guard the southern defile.

sourceUnits.zh: 翰與釗戰於木底，大敗之，乘勝遂入丸都，釗單馬而遁。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han routed him at Mudi, pressed into Wandu, and Zhao fled alone on horseback.
sourceUnits.literal: Han fought Zhao at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode victory then entered Wandu; Zhao single horse fled.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝掘釗父利墓，載其屍並其母妻珍寶，掠男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都而歸。
sourceUnits.en: Huang opened Gao Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhao’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, razed Wandu, and returned.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang dug Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, loaded his corpse together with his mother, wife, and treasures, plundered over fifty thousand male and female, burned his palace chambers, destroyed Wandu and returned.

sourceUnits.zh: 明年，釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍。
sourceUnits.en: The next year Gao Zhao sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
sourceUnits.literal: The next year, Zhao sent envoys declaring subject to Huang, offered their local products, then returned his father’s corpse.

sourceUnits.zh: 宇文歸遣其國相莫淺渾伐皝，諸將請戰，皝不許。
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent Moqian Hun; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
sourceUnits.literal: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; the generals requested battle; Huang did not permit.

sourceUnits.zh: 渾以皝為憚之，荒酒縱獵，不復設備。
sourceUnits.en: Moqian Hun assumed Huang was afraid and gave himself to drink and hunting without precautions.
sourceUnits.literal: Hun because Huang feared them, indulged wine and wantonly hunted, again did not set defenses.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝曰：「渾奢忌已甚，今則可一戰矣。」
sourceUnits.en: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s arrogance has peaked—now we can strike.”
sourceUnits.literal: Huang said: “Hun’s extravagance and jealousy are already extreme; now then can one battle.”

sourceUnits.zh: 遣翰率騎擊之，渾大敗，僅以身免，盡俘其眾。
sourceUnits.en: He sent Murong Han with cavalry to strike them; Moqian Hun was badly defeated and escaped alone, while his entire host was taken captive.
sourceUnits.literal: Sent Han leading cavalry to strike them; Hun was greatly defeated, barely himself escaped, wholly captured their host.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝躬巡郡縣，勸課農桑，起龍城宮闕。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang toured his domains, pushed farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged and supervised farming and sericulture, raised Longcheng palace and towers.

sourceUnits.zh: 尋又率騎二萬親伐宇文歸，以翰及垂為前鋒。
sourceUnits.en: He soon took twenty thousand horse against Yuwen Gui, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van.
sourceUnits.literal: Soon again led cavalry twenty thousand personally to campaign against Yuwen Gui, with Han and Chui as vanguard.

sourceUnits.zh: 歸使其騎將涉奕於盡眾距翰，皝馳遣謂翰曰：「奕於雄悍，宜小避之，待虜勢驕，然後取也。」
sourceUnits.en: Yuwen Gui sent Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han; Huang sent word: “Sheyiyu is fierce—spar lightly until he grows reckless, then strike.”
sourceUnits.literal: Gui made his cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host to resist Han; Huang gallop-sent word telling Han: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; ought slightly to avoid him, wait until the bandits’ situation grows arrogant, then take them.”

sourceUnits.zh: 翰曰：「歸之精銳，盡在於此，今若克之，則歸可不勞兵而滅。
sourceUnits.en: Murong Han replied, “Yuwen Gui’s best troops are here; crush them and his realm falls without a long campaign.
sourceUnits.literal: Han said: “Gui’s picked troops are all here; now if we defeat them, then Gui can be destroyed without tiring the army.

sourceUnits.zh: 奕于徒有虛名，其實易與耳，不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣。」
sourceUnits.en: Sheyiyu is overrated and brittle—we must not let him sap our morale.”
sourceUnits.literal: Sheyiyu vainly has empty name; in truth he is easy to deal with; ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.”

sourceUnits.zh: 於是前戰，斬奕於，盡俘其眾，歸遠遁漠北。
sourceUnits.en: He attacked, slew Sheyiyu, took his army, and drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon advanced battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝開地千餘里，徙其部人五萬餘落于昌黎，改涉奕於城為威德城。
sourceUnits.en: He annexed a thousand li of pasture, resettled fifty thousand Yuwen dependents at Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu’s fort Weide.
sourceUnits.literal: Huang opened territory over a thousand li, moved their division people over fifty thousand settlements to Changli, changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.

sourceUnits.zh: 行飲至之禮，論功行賞各有差。
sourceUnits.en: He held a victory feast and handed out graded rewards.
sourceUnits.literal: Performed the “drink-on-arrival” rite, discussed merit and performed rewards each had gradations.

sourceUnits.zh: 以牧牛給貧家，田于苑中，公收其八，二分入私。
sourceUnits.en: Poor households received draft oxen to till the royal park on an eighty-twenty revenue split with the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Used herding oxen given to poor families, fields in the royal park, the public took eight-tenths, two-tenths went private.

sourceUnits.zh: 有牛而無地者，亦田苑中，公收其七，三分入私。
sourceUnits.en: Householders who owned cattle but no land tilled the park on a seventy-thirty split.
sourceUnits.literal: Those with oxen but without land, also fielded in the park, the public took seven-tenths, three-tenths went private.

sourceUnits.zh: 皝記室參軍封裕諫曰：臣聞聖王之宰國也，薄賦而藏于百姓，分之以三等之田，十一而稅之；
sourceUnits.en: Murong Huang's secretary Feng Yu remonstrated: I have heard that a sage king keeps taxes light and stores wealth among the people, divides land into three grades, and levies one part in ten;
sourceUnits.literal: Murong Huang's secretary-advisor Feng Yu remonstrated, saying: Your servant has heard that when a sage king governs a state, he keeps taxes light and stores wealth among the people, divides land into three grades, and levies one part in ten;
